players.product: DDR5 RCD / DB, MRDIMM MRCD / MDB, CXL memory-expander controllers and PCIe retimers

quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record): looking to next year, rising server CPU demand should lift overall memory-module demand and with it demand for memory-interface and module companion chips. PCIe Retimer shipments are mainly PCIe 5.0, with demand growth driven by rising domestic AI server demand. Management also cites the CXL route of attaching existing DDR4 to servers via MXC chips as a way for customers to cut memory-expansion cost while DDR prices rise.

Management (IR record): the DDR5 memory-interface chip generation has kept three suppliers (down from possibly more than 10 in DDR2, about 5 in DDR3 and 3 in DDR4); management says new entrants would struggle to affect the competitive landscape in the short to medium term given patents, JEDEC access and long CPU-maker / module-maker qualification cycles. Memory-interface chips work with any JEDEC-compliant server CPU, x86 or Arm; per public information, several North American cloud providers' in-house Arm CPUs support DDR5 modules and need memory-interface chips.
